Further broad sweeps or speculative microtuning are not justified by this evidence.

Material limits remain: body profiling covers one MakeUp natural-terrain tuple, not universal family costs. Nested intervals cannot be summed; mixed-scope lifecycle cannot be subtracted from fill; clock calibration is contextual. Native submission measures the CPU delegate chain, not GPU completion or isolated driver cost. Complementary startup remains a scoped blocker. Default enablement, live DH/PBR and broader quality/performance remain unqualified.

This closes the scoped research effort, not a successful speedup claim. I inspected existing code and evidence without rerunning tests, editing files, or delegating. N02–N04, previous goals and `docs/STATUS.md` remain untouched.

**CONTINUE — N01’s correctness/work requalification is supported, but the underlying optimization’s stopping rationale has one material gap.**

The remaining actionable step is **bounded profiling of the actual compaction/scalar path**, not further guard weakening or another broad family sweep.

- The [latest Solas result](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/dev/experiments/new-optimization-goals-20261102/n01-solas-natural-affinity-r1-interpretation.json) fails to repeat the earlier gain and reports candidate CPU time above both controls. [Bliss’s refined-loop repeat](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/dev/experiments/new-optimization-goals-20261102/n01-bliss-natural-affinity-r2-interpretation.json) also establishes no gain. These observations justify investigating cost, but do **not** causally identify the algorithm as responsible.
- The existing cost observer wraps only admission predicates in [MakeUpQuadRuntime.java](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/integration/makeupquad/MakeUpQuadRuntime.java:152). It excludes the actual validation/planning and mutation passes, scalar publication, and native submission. Its small measured cost supports retaining safety checks; it cannot establish that material improvement opportunities in those bodies are exhausted.
- Source inspection confirms [AdjacentQuadCoalescer.java](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/integration/makeupquad/AdjacentQuadCoalescer.java) still performs whole-batch planning followed by mutation when merging. That is justified for correctness, but its actual cost remains unmeasured. Reduced command counts alone cannot resolve the trade-off.

**Next work:** add a separate, bounded diagnostic through the maintained harness on one already-qualified natural-terrain tuple. Attribute actual compactor, scalar lifecycle and surrounding native submission cost, accounting for instrumentation overhead and keeping scored windows uninstrumented. Preserve all mutable guards and restoration. Refine only if this identifies a material, safely removable cost; otherwise use the measured small cost or concrete attribution limit to support stopping. No exhaustive hardware/preset search is needed.

I found no blocking correctness defect in the inspected loop/cache changes. The [33-test evidence](/home/philip/ShaderLOD/dev/experiments/new-optimization-goals-20261102/n01-coalescer-loop-tests/summary.json) supports stream/max/publication behavior, and inspected maintained summaries support restoration. Complementary startup remains a scoped runtime blocker; DH/PBR and default enablement remain unqualified.

This verdict concerns **underlying N01**, not reopening the accepted scoped reviews. I inspected existing evidence without rerunning tests or modifying files; N02–N04 and previous goals remain untouched.
